title: Singular high-harmonic transport above a quantum threshold
authors: Yugo Onishi, Su-Yang Xu, Liang Fu
abstract: We show that Landau-Zener tunneling in a small-gap insulator produces a singular DC current--voltage relation, and correspondingly, strong high-harmonic generation in AC transport. Remarkably, high-harmonic responses decrease subexponentially with harmonic order, which is parametrically slower than in ordinary conductors and PN diodes. We further derive a scaling law for the current amplitude at frequency $nω$ produced by the applied electric field $E$ at fundamental frequency $ω$. Our work offers a promising route to THz generation based on frequency multiplication in solids.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes the strong-field transport in band insulators exhibiting a quantum power threshold. It shows that the resulting singular current-voltage relation generates high-harmonic radiation whose amplitude decays sub-exponentially. The authors derive universal scaling laws governing these harmonics, offering a pathway for THz generation in solids.
main_problem: The paper investigates the nonperturbative, strong-field transport in band insulators, specifically characterizing the singular high-harmonic generation resulting from a quantum power threshold.
main_result: The current exhibits a singular DC-voltage relation due to Landau-Zener tunneling, leading to high-harmonic generation whose amplitude decays sub-exponentially with harmonic order, following a derived scaling law.
method: The analysis uses the quantum master equation in the steady state, followed by Fourier analysis and the saddle-point approximation to derive asymptotic scaling laws for the harmonic components.
model_or_system: The model is a small-gap insulator, initially treated as a 1D system governed by a massive Dirac Hamiltonian. Transport is driven by interband tunneling, characterized by a quantum power threshold $w_Q$.
key_observables: DC current-voltage relation $J(E)$, and the high-harmonic current amplitudes $J_n$ at frequency $n\omega$.
important_parameters: The quantum power threshold $w_Q = \Delta^2/\hbar$, and the characteristic field scale $E_c = \pi\Delta^2 / \hbar v e$.
main_assumptions: Approximations include the relaxation time approximation (RTA) and the use of the saddle-point method for evaluating Fourier integrals, assuming the main contribution comes from the singularity near $E=0$.
figures_summary: Figures compare the calculated $J-V$ relation to numerical solutions, contrast the sub-exponential decay of harmonics from singular transport against super-exponential decay from analytic models, and illustrate the collapse of harmonic amplitudes onto a universal scaling function.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the singular DC current-voltage relation via Landau-Zener tunneling in a 1D model, then extends this to AC transport by analyzing the Fourier components, deriving universal scaling laws, and comparing these results to other transport regimes.
why_interesting: The study of non-equilibrium, strong-field quantum transport, particularly the emergence of universal scaling laws for high harmonics, connects fundamental quantum tunneling physics to observable THz generation phenomena.

We note that the enhancement of the high harmonics and the scaling law originate from a current–voltage re- lation with a sharp onset behavior, and we expect that they do not depend on details of the singularity in the current–voltage relation (also see SM). Higher dimensions. — Higher-dimensional systems can be treated as families of 1D momentum-space slices. In contrast to 1D cases, the singular response survives when the full system is gapless at an isolated point, be- cause almost all slices retain a finite effective gap.
